sanskrit: sphītāṃś ca śāliyavasair haṃsasārasasevitān padminībhiś ca śataśaḥ śrīmatībhir alaṃkṛtān
english: He passed teeming lands rich with rice and barley, frequented by swans and cranes, and adorned by the hundreds with stately, beautiful lotus-pools.

sanskrit: sa videhān atikramya samṛddhajanasevitān mithilopavanaṃ ramyam āsasāda maharddhimat
english: Having crossed through the Videha country, thronged with prosperous folk, he reached the lovely, richly endowed pleasure-grove of Mithilā.

sanskrit: hastyaśvarathasaṃkīrṇaṃ naranārīsamākulam paśyann apaśyann iva tat samatikrāmad acyutaḥ
english: Crowded with elephants, horses, and chariots, thronging with men and women — the steadfast one passed through it, seeing it yet as though he saw it not.

sanskrit: manasā taṃ vahan bhāraṃ tam evārthaṃ vicintayan ātmārāmaḥ prasannātmā mithilām āsasāda ha
english: Bearing that burden in his mind and pondering that single aim, delighting in the Self, serene of spirit, he came at last to Mithilā.

sanskrit: tasyā dvāraṃ samāsādya dvārapālair nivāritaḥ sthito dhyānaparo mukto viditaḥ praviveśa ha
english: Reaching her gate, he was barred by the gatekeepers; rapt in meditation he stood, the liberated one, and only when recognized did he enter.

sanskrit: sa rājamārgam āsādya samṛddhajanasaṃkulam pārthivakṣayam āsādya niḥśaṅkaḥ praviveśa ha
english: Coming to the royal highway, crowded with prosperous people, and reaching the king's palace, without hesitation he entered in.

sanskrit: tatrāpi dvārapālās tam ugravāco nyaṣedhayan tathaiva ca śukas tatra nirmanyuḥ samatiṣṭhata
english: There too the gatekeepers with harsh words forbade him, and Śuka, free of all anger, simply stood his ground.

sanskrit: na cātapādhvasaṃtaptaḥ kṣutpipāsāśramānvitaḥ pratāmyati glāyati vā nāpaiti ca tathātapāt
english: Though scorched by sun and road, beset by hunger, thirst, and weariness, he neither grew faint nor wilted, nor did he withdraw from that heat.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tu dvārapālānām ekaḥ śokasamanvitaḥ madhyaṃgatam ivādityaṃ dṛṣṭvā śukam avasthitam
english: But one of those gatekeepers, filled with compassion, beheld Śuka standing there like the sun arrived at its zenith.

sanskrit: pūjayitvā yathānyāyam abhivādya kṛtāñjaliḥ prāveśayat tataḥ kakṣyāṃ dvitīyāṃ rājaveśmanaḥ
english: Having honored him as was fitting and saluted him with folded hands, he led him then into the second court of the king's palace.

sanskrit: tatrāsīnaḥ śukas tāta mokṣam evānucintayan chāyāyām ātape caiva samadarśī mahādyutiḥ
english: Seated there, my child, Śuka of great splendor pondered liberation alone, looking with equal eye upon shade and upon sun.

sanskrit: taṃ muhūrtād ivāgamya rājño mantrī kṛtāñjaliḥ prāveśayat tataḥ kakṣyāṃ tṛtīyāṃ rājaveśmanaḥ
english: After but a moment the king's minister came to him with folded hands and led him into the third court of the king's palace.

sanskrit: tatrāntaḥpurasaṃbaddhaṃ mahac caitrarathopamam suvibhaktajalākrīḍaṃ ramyaṃ puṣpitapādapam
english: There, adjoining the inner apartments, was a great park like Citraratha's own, with well-laid bathing-pools, lovely, its trees in flower.

sanskrit: tad darśayitvā sa śukaṃ mantrī kānanam uttamam arham āsanam ādiśya niścakrāma tataḥ punaḥ
english: Having shown Śuka that finest of groves and appointed him a worthy seat, the minister then withdrew once more.

sanskrit: taṃ cāruveṣāḥ suśroṇyas taruṇyaḥ priyadarśanāḥ sūkṣmaraktāmbaradharās taptakāñcanabhūṣaṇāḥ
english: Then young women, fair to behold, in graceful attire, shapely of hip, clad in fine red garments and decked in refined gold ornaments,

sanskrit: saṃlāpollāpakuśalā nṛttagītaviśāradāḥ smitapūrvābhibhāṣiṇyo rūpeṇāpsarasāṃ samāḥ
english: skilled in converse and witty repartee, accomplished in dance and song, speaking always with a smile, in beauty the equals of the apsarases —

sanskrit: kāmopacārakuśalā bhāvajñāḥ sarvakovidāḥ paraṃ pañcāśato nāryo vāramukhyāḥ samādravan
english: adept in the arts of love, reading every mood, accomplished in all things — these chief courtesans, more than fifty women, came hastening near.

sanskrit: pādyādīni pratigrāhya pūjayā parayārcya ca deśakālopapannena sādhvannenāpy atarpayan
english: Receiving him with water for his feet and the rest, honoring him with the highest reverence, they refreshed him too with wholesome food befitting the place and the hour.

sanskrit: tasya bhuktavatas tāta tad antaḥpurakānanam suramyaṃ darśayām āsur ekaikaśyena bhārata
english: When he had eaten, my child, they showed him that delightful garden of the inner court, O Bhārata, one part after another.

sanskrit: krīḍantyaś ca hasantyaś ca gāyantyaś caiva tāḥ śukam udārasattvaṃ sattvajñāḥ sarvāḥ paryacaraṃs tadā
english: Sporting and laughing and singing, those women, all skilled in the ways of the heart, then waited upon Śuka of noble spirit.

sanskrit: āraṇeyas tu śuddhātmā trisaṃdehas trikarmakṛt vaśyendriyo jitakrodho na hṛṣyati na kupyati
english: But the son of the fire-sticks, pure of soul, free of the three doubts, performer of the threefold rite, his senses mastered and his anger conquered, neither rejoiced nor grew wroth.

sanskrit: tasmai śayyāsanaṃ divyaṃ varārhaṃ ratnabhūṣitam spardhyāstaraṇasaṃstīrṇaṃ dadus tāḥ paramastriyaḥ
english: To him those choice women gave a divine couch and seat, worthy of the best, jeweled and spread with coverlets such as men contend to own.

sanskrit: pādaśaucaṃ tu kṛtvaiva śukaḥ saṃdhyām upāsya ca niṣasādāsane puṇye tam evārthaṃ vicintayan
english: Having washed his feet and worshiped at the twilight hour, Śuka sat down upon that holy seat, pondering still that single aim.

sanskrit: pūrvarātre tu tatrāsau bhūtvā dhyānaparāyaṇaḥ madhyarātre yathānyāyaṃ nidrām āhārayat prabhuḥ
english: In the first watch of the night he gave himself wholly to meditation; at midnight, as was proper, that self-possessed one took his sleep.

sanskrit: tato muhūrtād utthāya kṛtvā śaucam anantaram strībhiḥ parivṛto dhīmān dhyānam evānvapadyata
english: Then, rising after a brief while and at once performing his ablutions, the wise one, though surrounded by women, betook himself again to meditation alone.

sanskrit: anena vidhinā kārṣṇis tad ahaḥśeṣam acyutaḥ tāṃ ca rātriṃ nṛpakule vartayām āsa bhārata
english: In this manner the steadfast son of Kṛṣṇa-Dvaipāyana passed the remainder of that day and that night within the royal household, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tataḥ sa rājā janako mantribhiḥ saha bhārata puraḥ purohitaṃ kṛtvā sarvāṇy antaḥpurāṇi ca
english: Bhīṣma said: Then, O Bhārata, that king Janaka, together with his ministers, putting his household priest at the fore and all the women of the inner apartments,

sanskrit: āsanaṃ ca puraskṛtya ratnāni vividhāni ca śirasā cārghyam ādāya guruputraṃ samabhyagāt
english: and bearing before him a seat, and jewels of many kinds, and carrying the welcome-offering upon his head, drew near to the teacher's son.

sanskrit: sa tad āsanam ādāya bahuratnavibhūṣitam spardhyāstaraṇasaṃstīrṇaṃ sarvatobhadram ṛddhimat
english: Taking up that seat, adorned with many jewels, spread with enviable coverlets, auspicious on every side and richly wrought,

sanskrit: purodhasā saṃgṛhītaṃ hastenālabhya pārthivaḥ pradadau guruputrāya śukāya paramārcitam
english: which the priest held ready — the king, touching it with his hand, gave it, most reverently honored, to the teacher's son Śuka.

sanskrit: tatropaviṣṭaṃ taṃ kārṣṇiṃ śāstrataḥ pratyapūjayat pādyaṃ nivedya prathamam arghyaṃ gāṃ ca nyavedayat sa ca tāṃ mantravat pūjāṃ pratyagṛhṇād yathāvidhi
english: When the son of Kṛṣṇa-Dvaipāyana had taken his seat there, the king honored him according to the scriptures: offering first water for his feet, then the welcome-draught and a cow; and Śuka received that worship with its sacred verses in due form.

sanskrit: pratigṛhya ca tāṃ pūjāṃ janakād dvijasattamaḥ gāṃ caiva samanujñāya rājānam anumānya ca
english: And having accepted that worship from Janaka, the best of the twice-born gave leave for the cow to be spared, and showing honor to the king,

sanskrit: paryapṛcchan mahātejā rājñaḥ kuśalam avyayam anāmayaṃ ca rājendra śukaḥ sānucarasya ha
english: Śuka of great brilliance inquired, O lord of kings, after the king's welfare, his unfailing prosperity and his health, and that of his retinue as well.

sanskrit: anujñātaḥ sa tenātha niṣasāda sahānugaḥ udārasattvābhijano bhūmau rājā kṛtāñjaliḥ
english: Then, granted leave by him, the king of noble nature and high lineage sat down upon the ground with his attendants, his hands folded in reverence.

sanskrit: kuśalaṃ cāvyayaṃ caiva pṛṣṭvā vaiyāsakiṃ nṛpaḥ kim āgamanam ity eva paryapṛcchata pārthivaḥ
english: And the king, having inquired after the welfare and well-being of Vyāsa's son, then asked him this: 'What is the purpose of your coming?'

sanskrit: śuka uvāca pitrāham ukto bhadraṃ te mokṣadharmārthakovidaḥ videharājo yājyo me janako nāma viśrutaḥ
english: Śuka said: My father told me — blessings upon you — 'The king of Videha, renowned as Janaka, is one for whom I have officiated, and he is versed in the law and aim of liberation.

sanskrit: tatra gacchasva vai tūrṇaṃ yadi te hṛdi saṃśayaḥ pravṛttau vā nivṛttau vā sa te chetsyati saṃśayam
english: Go to him at once, if any doubt lingers in your heart, whether concerning action or withdrawal from action; he will cut your doubt away.'

sanskrit: so 'haṃ pitur niyogāt tvām upapraṣṭum ihāgataḥ tan me dharmabhṛtāṃ śreṣṭha yathāvad vaktum arhasi
english: So I, at my father's bidding, have come here to question you; therefore, O best of those who uphold the law, you should tell me truly:

sanskrit: kiṃ kāryaṃ brāhmaṇeneha mokṣārthaś ca kim ātmakaḥ kathaṃ ca mokṣaḥ kartavyo jñānena tapasāpi vā
english: What ought a brāhmaṇa to do in this world, and of what nature is the aim of liberation? And how is liberation to be attained — by knowledge, or by austerity?

sanskrit: janaka uvāca yat kāryaṃ brāhmaṇeneha janmaprabhṛti tac chṛṇu kṛtopanayanas tāta bhaved vedaparāyaṇaḥ
english: Janaka said: Hear, then, what a brāhmaṇa ought to do in this world from his birth onward. Once invested with the sacred thread, my child, he should be wholly devoted to the Veda;

sanskrit: tapasā guruvṛttyā ca brahmacaryeṇa cābhibho devatānāṃ pitṝṇāṃ cāpy anṛṇaś cānasūyakaḥ
english: by austerity, by service to his teacher, and by chastity, O mighty one, he becomes free of debt to the gods and to the ancestors, and free of all envy.

sanskrit: vedān adhītya niyato dakṣiṇām apavarjya ca abhyanujñām atha prāpya samāvarteta vai dvijaḥ
english: Having studied the Vedas, self-controlled, and having bestowed the teacher's fee, and then obtaining leave, the twice-born one should return home from his studentship.

sanskrit: samāvṛttas tu gārhasthye sadāro niyato vaset anasūyur yathānyāyam āhitāgnis tathaiva ca
english: Having returned, he should dwell in the householder's state, self-restrained and with a wife, free of envy, and, as is proper, keeping the sacred fires kindled.

sanskrit: utpādya putrapautraṃ tu vanyāśramapade vaset tān evāgnīn yathāśāstram arcayann atithipriyaḥ
english: And having begotten sons and grandsons, he should dwell in the abode of the forest hermitage, tending those same fires as the scriptures prescribe, and welcoming guests gladly.

sanskrit: sa vane 'gnīn yathānyāyam ātmany āropya dharmavit nirdvaṃdvo vītarāgātmā brahmāśramapade vaset
english: Then in the forest, the knower of dharma, having in due form laid those fires within his own self, beyond the pairs of opposites and freed of passion, should dwell in the abode of the renunciant devoted to Brahman.

sanskrit: śuka uvāca utpanne jñānavijñāne pratyakṣe hṛdi śāśvate kim avaśyaṃ nivastavyam āśrameṣu vaneṣu ca
english: Śuka said: When knowledge and discernment have arisen, immediate and abiding within the heart, must one then perforce dwell through the orders of life and in the forests?

sanskrit: etad bhavantaṃ pṛcchāmi tad bhavān vaktum arhati yathāvedārthatattvena brūhi me tvaṃ janādhipa
english: This I ask of you, and you should answer it; tell me, O ruler of men, in accord with the very truth of the Veda's meaning.

sanskrit: janaka uvāca na vinā jñānavijñānaṃ mokṣasyādhigamo bhavet na vinā gurusaṃbandhaṃ jñānasyādhigamaḥ smṛtaḥ
english: Janaka said: Without knowledge and discernment there can be no attaining of liberation; and without the bond with a teacher, no attaining of knowledge is taught.

sanskrit: ācāryaḥ plāvitā tasya jñānaṃ plava ihocyate vijñāya kṛtakṛtyas tu tīrṇas tad ubhayaṃ tyajet
english: The teacher is the ferryman, and knowledge is here called the raft; but once he has understood and accomplished his task, having crossed over, he should let both go.

sanskrit: anucchedāya lokānām anucchedāya karmaṇām pūrvair ācarito dharmaś cāturāśramyasaṃkathaḥ
english: For the unbroken continuance of the worlds and the unbroken continuance of rites, the dharma told of in the teaching of the four orders of life was practiced by the ancients.

sanskrit: anena kramayogena bahujātiṣu karmaṇā kṛtvā śubhāśubhaṃ karma mokṣo nāmeha labhyate
english: By this disciplined sequence, through many births, having performed both good and ill deeds, what is called liberation is here attained.

sanskrit: bhavitaiḥ kāraṇaiś cāyaṃ bahusaṃsārayoniṣu āsādayati śuddhātmā mokṣaṃ vai prathamāśrame
english: Through causes ripened in many wombs of recurring existence, this man of purified soul reaches liberation even in the first order of life.

sanskrit: tam āsādya tu muktasya dṛṣṭārthasya vipaścitaḥ triṣv āśrameṣu ko nv artho bhavet param abhīpsataḥ
english: But for one who has attained it — liberated, having seen the truth, wise, and longing for the supreme — what need is there of the three remaining orders of life?

sanskrit: rājasāṃs tāmasāṃś caiva nityaṃ doṣān vivarjayet sāttvikaṃ mārgam āsthāya paśyed ātmānam ātmanā
english: Let him ever shun the faults born of passion and of darkness; treading the path of purity, let him behold the Self by the self.

sanskrit: sarvabhūteṣu cātmānaṃ sarvabhūtāni cātmani saṃpaśyan nopalipyeta jale vāricaro yathā
english: Seeing the Self in all beings and all beings within the Self, he is not tainted, as the water-creature is not wetted by the water.

sanskrit: pakṣīva plavanād ūrdhvam amutrānantyam aśnute vihāya dehaṃ nirmukto nirdvaṃdvaḥ praśamaṃ gataḥ
english: Like a bird soaring up in flight, he wins endlessness in the world beyond; casting off the body, released, beyond the pairs of opposites, he attains to perfect peace.

sanskrit: atra gāthāḥ purā gītāḥ śṛṇu rājñā yayātinā dhāryante yā dvijais tāta mokṣaśāstraviśāradaiḥ
english: On this, hear the verses sung of old by King Yayāti, which, my child, are held in memory by the twice-born skilled in the science of liberation.

sanskrit: jyotir ātmani nānyatra rataṃ tatraiva caiva tat svayaṃ ca śakyaṃ tad draṣṭuṃ susamāhitacetasā
english: The light is within the Self, nowhere else, and it delights in that alone; and it can be seen of oneself by a mind well composed.

sanskrit: na bibheti paro yasmān na bibheti parāc ca yaḥ yaś ca necchati na dveṣṭi brahma saṃpadyate tadā
english: He of whom no other is afraid, and who fears no other, and who neither craves nor hates — then he becomes Brahman.

sanskrit: yadā bhāvaṃ na kurute sarvabhūteṣu pāpakam karmaṇā manasā vācā brahma saṃpadyate tadā
english: When he harbors no evil intent toward any being, in deed, in thought, or in word — then he becomes Brahman.

sanskrit: saṃyojya tapasātmānam īrṣyām utsṛjya mohinīm tyaktvā kāmaṃ ca lobhaṃ ca tato brahmatvam aśnute
english: Yoking the self by austerity, casting off bewildering envy, and abandoning desire and greed — thereupon he attains to the state of Brahman.

sanskrit: yadā śravye ca dṛśye ca sarvabhūteṣu cāpyayam samo bhavati nirdvaṃdvo brahma saṃpadyate tadā
english: When toward all that is heard and seen, and toward all beings and their dissolution, he becomes the same, beyond the pairs of opposites — then he becomes Brahman.

sanskrit: yadā stutiṃ ca nindāṃ ca samatvenaiva paśyati kāñcanaṃ cāyasaṃ caiva sukhaduḥkhe tathaiva ca
english: When he looks with equal eye upon praise and blame alike, upon gold and upon iron, and upon pleasure and pain the same,

sanskrit: śītam uṣṇaṃ tathaivārtham anarthaṃ priyam apriyam jīvitaṃ maraṇaṃ caiva brahma saṃpadyate tadā
english: upon cold and heat, upon gain and loss, the dear and the unwelcome, upon life and death alike — then he becomes Brahman.

sanskrit: prasāryeha yathāṅgāni kūrmaḥ saṃharate punaḥ tathendriyāṇi manasā saṃyantavyāni bhikṣuṇā
english: As a tortoise, having stretched forth its limbs here, draws them in again, so should the mendicant restrain the senses by the mind.

sanskrit: tamaḥparigataṃ veśma yathā dīpena dṛśyate tathā buddhipradīpena śakya ātmā nirīkṣitum
english: As a house enveloped in darkness is made visible by a lamp, so by the lamp of the intellect can the Self be perceived.

sanskrit: etat sarvaṃ prapaśyāmi tvayi buddhimatāṃ vara yac cānyad api vettavyaṃ tattvato veda tad bhavān
english: All this I see in you, O best of the wise; and whatever else there is to be known, that too you know in its very truth.

sanskrit: brahmarṣe viditaś cāsi viṣayāntam upāgataḥ guros tava prasādena tava caivopaśikṣayā
english: O brāhmaṇa-sage, you are known to me as one who has reached the end of all objects of sense, by the grace of your teacher and by your own diligent learning.

sanskrit: tasyaiva ca prasādena prādurbhūtaṃ mahāmune jñānaṃ divyaṃ mamāpīdaṃ tenāsi vidito mama
english: And by that same grace, O great sage, this divine knowledge has arisen in me also; therefore are you known to me.

sanskrit: adhikaṃ tava vijñānam adhikā ca gatis tava adhikaṃ ca tavaiśvaryaṃ tac ca tvaṃ nāvabudhyase
english: Greater is your discernment, and higher your attainment, and greater your sovereign power — yet of this you yourself are not aware.

sanskrit: bālyād vā saṃśayād vāpi bhayād vāpy avimokṣajāt utpanne cāpi vijñāne nādhigacchati tāṃ gatim
english: Whether through immaturity, or doubt, or fear born of not yet being released, a man may fail to reach that goal even when discernment has arisen.

sanskrit: vyavasāyena śuddhena madvidhaiś chinnasaṃśayaḥ vimucya hṛdayagranthīn āsādayati tāṃ gatim
english: But with pure resolve, his doubt severed by such as I am, loosing the knots of the heart, he attains that goal.

sanskrit: bhavāṃś cotpannavijñānaḥ sthirabuddhir alolupaḥ vyavasāyād ṛte brahmann āsādayati tatparam
english: And you, in whom discernment has arisen, steadfast of mind and free of craving — even without such resolve, O brāhmaṇa, you attain that supreme state.

sanskrit: nāsti te sukhaduḥkheṣu viśeṣo nāsti lolupā nautsukyaṃ nṛttagīteṣu na rāga upajāyate
english: For you there is no distinction in pleasures and pains, there is no craving; no eagerness for dance and song, and no passion arises in you.

sanskrit: na bandhuṣu nibandhas te na bhayeṣv asti te bhayam paśyāmi tvāṃ mahābhāga tulyaloṣṭāśmakāñcanam
english: You have no bondage to kinsmen, and amid terrors there is no fear in you; I see you, O greatly blessed one, holding a clod, a stone, and gold as all alike.

sanskrit: ahaṃ ca tvānupaśyāmi ye cāpy anye manīṣiṇaḥ āsthitaṃ paramaṃ mārgam akṣayaṃ tam anāmayam
english: I, and the other thinkers as well, behold you as having entered upon the supreme path, the imperishable and the free of all affliction.

sanskrit: yat phalaṃ brāhmaṇasyeha mokṣārthaś ca yad ātmakaḥ tasmin vai vartase vipra kim anyat paripṛcchasi
english: That which is the fruit of a brāhmaṇa's life here, and of what nature is the aim of liberation — in that very state you abide, O brāhmaṇa; what more do you ask?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca etac chrutvā tu vacanaṃ kṛtātmā kṛtaniścayaḥ ātmanātmānam āsthāya dṛṣṭvā cātmānam ātmanā
english: Bhīṣma said: Having heard this counsel, the perfected one, his resolve now firm, taking his stand upon the Self by the self, and beholding the Self by the self,

sanskrit: kṛtakāryaḥ sukhī śāntas tūṣṇīṃ prāyād udaṅmukhaḥ śaiśiraṃ girim uddiśya sadharmā mātariśvanaḥ
english: his purpose accomplished, happy and at peace, set forth in silence facing the north, making for the snow-clad mountain, of a nature like unto the Wind.

sanskrit: etasminn eva kāle tu devarṣir nāradas tadā himavantam iyād draṣṭuṃ siddhacāraṇasevitam
english: And at that very time the divine sage Nārada was on his way to behold the Himavat, frequented by the perfected ones and the celestial wanderers.
